scenes.tts: Two cells carry the same genome. Why can they read different genes? Watch one gene in each nucleus. The D N A sequence matches. Yet one cell makes many messenger R N A molecules, while the other makes almost none. The puzzle is not missing genes. It is selective use.
scenes.caption: Two cells carry the same genome. Why can they read different genes? Watch one gene in each nucleus. The DNA sequence matches. Yet one cell makes many messenger RNA molecules, while the other makes almost none. The puzzle is not missing genes. It is selective use.
scenes.visual: Open immediately on a 16:9 split screen labelled 'liver cell' and 'kidney cell'. Each nucleus contains the same large schematic gene. Establish and retain this colour map in both films: BLUE DNA, GOLD nucleosomes, WHITE promoter, TEAL enhancer, GREEN regulators, MAGENTA DNA-methylation tags, pale-grey RNA. The left gene releases a moving stream of pale-grey RNA strokes; the right releases almost none. Keep a small 'schematic' label visible. The paired genes fill over sixty percent of frame height.
scenes.narration: Two cells carry the same genome. Why can they read different genes? Watch one gene in each nucleus. The DNA sequence matches. Yet one cell makes many messenger RNA molecules, while the other makes almost none. The puzzle is not missing genes. It is selective use.

scenes.visual: Over the still-moving split nuclei, fade in the title 'Access, Then Assembly'. Gold nucleosomes drift slowly along both blue DNA ribbons, and pale-grey RNA continues moving on the left. Fade the title before the next scene.

scenes.tts: Eukaryotic D N A is packed into chromatin. Blue D N A wraps around gold nucleosomes. Packing does not make every gene permanently silent. It makes access conditional. Proteins must reach the promoter before transcription can begin. Packed D N A is harder, not impossible, to read.
scenes.caption: Eukaryotic DNA is packed into chromatin. Blue DNA wraps around gold nucleosomes. Packing does not make every gene permanently silent. It makes access conditional. Proteins must reach the promoter before transcription can begin. Packed DNA is harder, not impossible, to read.
scenes.visual: Merge the split screen into one enlarged blue DNA ribbon crossing the frame. Gold labelled blocks marked 'nucleosome' gather the ribbon around themselves without molecular detail. A white promoter slot appears beneath one nucleosome. A large transcription block approaches, bumps gently into the wrapped segment, and waits. The word 'conditional' replaces a briefly shown open-or-shut toggle.
scenes.narration: Eukaryotic DNA is packed into chromatin. Blue DNA wraps around gold nucleosomes. Packing does not make every gene permanently silent. It makes access conditional. Proteins must reach the promoter before transcription can begin. Packed DNA is harder, not impossible, to read.

scenes.tts: Remodelling complexes can move nucleosomes. As one gold block slides aside, the white promoter becomes reachable. Some pioneer factors can bind nucleosomal D N A, so access and regulator binding can influence each other. The promoter stays fixed while nucleosomes shift around it.
scenes.caption: Remodelling complexes can move nucleosomes. As one gold block slides aside, the white promoter becomes reachable. Some pioneer factors can bind nucleosomal DNA, so access and regulator binding can influence each other. The promoter stays fixed while nucleosomes shift around it.
scenes.visual: A labelled block 'remodeller' pushes the gold nucleosome along the carried blue ribbon. The white promoter opens into view, and the waiting transcription block fits into it. Then show one small GREEN block labelled 'pioneer factor' settling on a separate wrapped segment. Use two curved arrows between 'access' and 'binding' to show mutual influence; do not show a fixed order.
scenes.narration: Remodelling complexes can move nucleosomes. As one gold block slides aside, the white promoter becomes reachable. Some pioneer factors can bind nucleosomal DNA, so access and regulator binding can influence each other. The promoter stays fixed while nucleosomes shift around it.

scenes.tts: Access is only one requirement. A teal enhancer can sit far from the promoter. Sequence-specific transcription factors bind the enhancer and recruit coactivators. Mediator helps connect these regulators with R N A polymerase two at the promoter. The enhancer itself is D N A, not a diffusible protein.
scenes.caption: Access is only one requirement. A teal enhancer can sit far from the promoter. Sequence-specific transcription factors bind the enhancer and recruit coactivators. Mediator helps connect these regulators with RNA polymerase II at the promoter. The enhancer itself is DNA, not a diffusible protein.
scenes.visual: Keep the promoter fixed at right and extend the same blue ribbon left to reveal a teal enhancer. GREEN factor blocks of two shapes dock at labelled sites. A GREEN coactivator block joins them. A labelled Mediator bridge grows toward the transcription block at the promoter while the intervening DNA bends into a broad arc. Label the contact 'usual picture; directness debated'.
scenes.narration: Access is only one requirement. A teal enhancer can sit far from the promoter. Sequence-specific transcription factors bind the enhancer and recruit coactivators. Mediator helps connect these regulators with RNA polymerase II at the promoter. The enhancer itself is DNA, not a diffusible protein.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Matching enhancer factors are present, but a nucleosome still covers the promoter. Is strong transcription guaranteed? Hold both requirements in view: regulatory assembly and access. Decide before the machinery moves.
scenes.caption: Now predict. Matching enhancer factors are present, but a nucleosome still covers the promoter. Is strong transcription guaranteed? Hold both requirements in view: regulatory assembly and access. Decide before the machinery moves.
scenes.visual: Freeze the carried gene at a decision point. GREEN factors occupy the TEAL enhancer at left. A GOLD nucleosome covers the WHITE promoter at right. Between them place a large question, 'Strong transcription guaranteed?' Under it, two equal labels glow alternately: 'regulators present' and 'promoter covered'. Ambient movement continues in the DNA arc.
scenes.narration: Now predict. Matching enhancer factors are present, but a nucleosome still covers the promoter. Is strong transcription guaranteed? Hold both requirements in view: regulatory assembly and access. Decide before the machinery moves.

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Keep 'Strong transcription guaranteed?' centred. The green factors pulse softly, the gold promoter nucleosome rocks slightly, and no RNA appears. Do not reveal an answer during the pause.

scenes.tts: No, not in this simplified case. The matching factors supply regulatory information, but the covered promoter remains hard to use. Bound factors can recruit a remodeller. Once it shifts the nucleosome, the assembled regulators can help raise transcription.
scenes.caption: No, not in this simplified case. The matching factors supply regulatory information, but the covered promoter remains hard to use. Bound factors can recruit a remodeller. Once it shifts the nucleosome, the assembled regulators can help raise transcription.
scenes.visual: Replace the question with 'not yet'. A GREEN factor at the enhancer recruits the labelled remodeller, which docks through that factor and then slides the gold block away, revealing the white promoter. Mediator completes the bridge, the transcription block engages, and a modest stream of pale-grey RNA strokes grows. Keep 'simplified case' and 'schematic' visible. Show the factors recruiting the remodeller; do not show the factors pushing the nucleosome themselves.
scenes.narration: No, not in this simplified case. The matching factors supply regulatory information, but the covered promoter remains hard to use. Bound factors can recruit a remodeller. Once it shifts the nucleosome, the assembled regulators can help raise transcription.

scenes.tts: Enhancers often act by combinations. Picture a committee whose decision depends on which members arrive. One factor alone may do little. Two together may recruit machinery effectively. Different cells supply different combinations.
scenes.caption: Enhancers often act by combinations. Picture a committee whose decision depends on which members arrive. One factor alone may do little. Two together may recruit machinery effectively. Different cells supply different combinations.
scenes.visual: Transform the TEAL enhancer into three large unlabelled docking sites, drawn as different shapes, with no letters and no numbers, so the film does not pre-solve the lesson's A, B, C deletion problem. Reset fully between cases. A single GREEN factor at one site produces a short RNA trickle. A single factor at another site also produces little. Two factors together complete a two-part docking shape and produce a larger schematic RNA stream. Label every readout 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Enhancers often act by combinations. Picture a committee whose decision depends on which members arrive. One factor alone may do little. Two together may recruit machinery effectively. Different cells supply different combinations.

scenes.tts: Return to the two cells. Their D N A still matches. In the liver cell, the needed factors and accessible promoter coincide. In the kidney cell, a needed factor may be missing. A repressor could also explain low output.
scenes.caption: Return to the two cells. Their DNA still matches. In the liver cell, the needed factors and accessible promoter coincide. In the kidney cell, a needed factor may be missing. A repressor could also explain low output.
scenes.visual: Split the carried gene back into matching liver and kidney copies. In liver, both GREEN factor shapes dock and the WHITE promoter remains visible. In kidney, leave one factor position as a question-mark outline; then add a separate possible GREEN-outlined block labelled 'repressor?' without choosing it. Use 'may be missing' and 'also fits' on screen. RNA streams stay clearly schematic.
scenes.narration: Return to the two cells. Their DNA still matches. In the liver cell, the needed factors and accessible promoter coincide. In the kidney cell, a needed factor may be missing. A repressor could also explain low output.

scenes.tts: A reporter assay can test these pieces beside a promoter. Deleting a piece tests necessity, and testing it alone tests sufficiency. Combining pieces tests cooperation, and reversing one tests orientation. But the assay moves D N A from its native setting. A genomic deletion is a stronger test there.
scenes.caption: A reporter assay can test these pieces beside a promoter. Deleting a piece tests necessity, and testing it alone tests sufficiency. Combining pieces tests cooperation, and reversing one tests orientation. But the assay moves DNA from its native setting. A genomic deletion is a stronger test there.
scenes.visual: The liver gene shrinks into a large reporter construct: TEAL enhancer pieces, WHITE promoter, and a pale-grey lamp labelled 'reporter'. In turn, with labels 'necessity', 'sufficiency', 'cooperation' and 'orientation': one piece lifts out, one piece stands alone, two pieces combine, and one piece flips; the lamp changes brightness without numbers. Then move the construct beside a faint chromosome silhouette labelled 'outside native setting'. Finish by highlighting one segment within the chromosome and labelling the possible test 'delete here'.
scenes.narration: A reporter assay can test these pieces beside a promoter. Deleting a piece tests necessity, and testing it alone tests sufficiency. Combining pieces tests cooperation, and reversing one tests orientation. But the assay moves DNA from its native setting. A genomic deletion is a stronger test there.

scenes.tts: The same genome can therefore support different outputs. Chromatin changes reachability. Enhancer-bound regulators change recruitment, including recruitment of enzymes that change reachability. Neither layer works as a universal switch. Together they make gene use conditional on cell state.
scenes.caption: The same genome can therefore support different outputs. Chromatin changes reachability. Enhancer-bound regulators change recruitment, including recruitment of enzymes that change reachability. Neither layer works as a universal switch. Together they make gene use conditional on cell state.
scenes.visual: Return to the large carried gene. GREEN regulators assemble on the TEAL enhancer and recruit the remodeller, which slides a GOLD nucleosome to reveal the WHITE promoter. Two arrows labelled 'access' and 'assembly' converge on a single moving RNA stream, with a small return arrow from 'assembly' to 'access'. Pull back to the liver and kidney nuclei, retaining different outputs but identical blue DNA.
scenes.narration: The same genome can therefore support different outputs. Chromatin changes reachability. Enhancer-bound regulators change recruitment, including recruitment of enzymes that change reachability. Neither layer works as a universal switch. Together they make gene use conditional on cell state.

scenes.visual: End card with one line only: 'Gene output depends on accessible DNA and the regulators present.' Keep the blue DNA ribbon, gold nucleosomes, teal enhancer, and green regulators moving faintly behind the centred line. Show no subtitle, logo, or second line.
